title: Quarterly Partnership Storyline + Deck Variants (Standard & Enterprise)
content:
Purpose:
This working doc contains a compact, modular QBR deck structure plus two ready-to-copy speaker-note variants: one optimized for Standard (self‑serve / SMB / product-led) accounts and one for Enterprise (SLA, exec-led, multi-stakeholder) accounts. Also includes a lightweight renewal-risk tracker, a scored risk rubric, and a short playbook for next steps and follow-ups.

How to use: 
- Pick the slide modules you need for the audience and time budget.
- Use the Standard speaker notes for technical or product-manager audiences; use Enterprise notes for executives and procurement stakeholders.
- Copy the renewal tracker table into a sheet for running updates between meetings.

Deck outline (modular slides) - total: 12–18 slides depending on depth
1. Title + Meeting Goal (30s)
   - One-line meeting purpose (e.g., "Align on outcomes, surface blockers, agree renewal timeline")
   - Attendees and roles (quick intro)

2. Executive snapshot (1 slide)
   - Top-line success metric (usage, ROI proxy, reliability)
   - Current renewal status (green/amber/red)
   - Ask / decision requested by end of QBR

3. Partnership highlights (1–2 slides)
   - Quick wins since last QBR (bullets)
   - Key integrations / milestones completed
   - Customer quote or NPS snippet

4. Adoption & Usage trends (1–2 slides)
   - Product usage chart (monthly active routes, tokens/day, embeddings volume)
   - Heavy-users versus marginal-users callouts

5. Reliability & Performance (1 slide)
   - Latency percentiles, error rate trend, major incidents since last QBR
   - For Enterprise: SLA attainment summary and mitigation actions

6. Cost & Efficiency (1 slide)
   - Unit cost per 1k tokens or per embedding, trend vs budget
   - Opportunities: batching, caching, quantization recommendations (one-line)

7. Quality & Risk (1 slide)
   - Output quality metrics (sample regressions, eval pass/fail)
   - Risk rubric score and short rationale

8. Roadmap & Product changes that matter (1 slide)
   - Upcoming infra or API changes that impact integration or cost

9. Success plan & Outcomes (1–2 slides)
   - Mutually agreed KPIs for next quarter (measurable targets)
   - Owner map for each KPI

10. Renewal discussion & timeline (1 slide)
   - Current contract end date, proposed renewal window, expansion opportunities

11. Concern log & mitigation (1 slide)
   - Open items, blockers, and committed next steps with owners and dates

12. Appendix / Technical deep-dive (optional)
   - Architecture snapshot, bench numbers, playbook for incident escalation

Speaker notes: Standard variant (short, product-focused)
- Title: "Set expectations: 30–45 minutes. We will surface adoption, performance, and next steps. Ask: agree on success KPIs and renewal timing."
- Executive snapshot: "Start with the single metric they care about (latency or cost savings) and a one-line example of where Redwood delivered value this quarter."
- Adoption: "Call out specific routes/features they use; show where usage is concentrated — helps identify where to target optimizations."
- Cost & Efficiency: "Keep this high level: "You're currently spending ~$X/month; with batching and caching we estimate 12–18% savings without quality loss.""
- Ask: "Confirm a 2-week window post-QBR to finalize renewal terms and identify an internal champion for procurement if needed."

Speaker notes: Enterprise variant (executive + procurement)
- Title: "This meeting is an executive alignment + decision checkpoint. Duration 45–60 minutes. Ask: verbal renewal intent + priority areas for contracting."
- Executive snapshot: "Include SLA attainment and any credits or remediation steps taken. If any incidents affected availability, briefly summarize RCA and long-term remediation."
- Reliability slide: "Highlight P99 latency, success rate, and incident MTTR. If remediation is in progress, show timeline and owners from SRE."
- Roadmap: "Prioritize items that reduce vendor risk or improve compliance (e.g., VPC/private deployment, KMS integration). Provide gating criteria for procurement to approve renewal."
- Pricing ask: "Outline proposed pricing tiers and enterprise discounts tied to committed monthly throughput or annual commit."

Renewal risk tracker (copy into Sheet for live updates):
| account | renewal_date | current_status | risk_score | top_risk_reason | next_action | owner | next_check_in |
| ACME Corp | 2025-03-15 | amber | 6/10 | procurement delay + SSO missing | schedule procurement call | María Gomez | 2025-01-22 |
| Beta Retail | 2025-04-01 | green | 2/10 | low usage growth | propose expansion pilot | Ethan Lewis | 2025-02-02 |

Risk scoring rubric (0–10, higher = more at-risk):
- 0–2: Confident, usage growing, exec sponsorship present
- 3–5: Some adoption gaps, minor procurement/legal blockers, no exec sign-off yet
- 6–8: Significant blockers (performance issues, cost concerns, procurement hold), needs action plan
- 9–10: Active churn risk or competitor replacing tech

Playbook: actions mapped to scores
- 0–2: Maintain cadence; run value-add sessions, share ROI report
- 3–5: Targeted enablement (onboarding deep-dive), propose limited discount tied to expansion commitment, schedule technical health check
- 6–8: Escalate to Solutions Eng and Senior CSM; propose dedicated bench/bridge support; set weekly risk standups
- 9–10: Exec-to-exec call, commercial special handling, legal review fast-track

Sample email templates (short):
- Pre-QBR invite (to send 2 weeks prior):
  Subject: QBR prep — Redwood + {{account}} (Proposed agenda + data request)
  Body: Hi {{name}}, want to confirm our QBR on {{date}}. Attached is a short agenda and a small data ask (usage CSV + top 3 business priorities). Aim: align on success metrics and renewal timeline.

- Post-QBR follow-up (24–48h):
  Subject: Follow‑up + agreed next steps from our QBR
  Body: Thanks for your time. Per our discussion: 1) KPI targets agreed: X, Y 2) Open items: SSO config (owner), procurement timeline. Next check-in: {{date}}. Attached: slide deck and playbook items.

Owner / RACI quick map (example)
- CSM: overall meeting lead, renewal choreography, exec intro
- Solutions Eng: technical deep-dive, remediation plan owners
- SRE/Infra: incident RCA and SLA actions (enterprise only)
- Sales AE: commercial terms, expansion proposals

Meeting checklist (CSM prep)
- Confirm attendee list and titles (execs vs PMs)
- Pull usage & billing snapshot (last 90 days)
- Annotate any incidents and remediation status
- Confirm legal/procurement readiness and gating items
- Attach product screenshots or evals that show impact

Common objections & suggested replies
- "Cost is too high": "We can run a 30‑day efficiency experiment (batching + sparse kv) and share post-run cost delta and quality comparison."
- "We had an outage": "Here's the RCA and a two-phase plan to prevent recurrence; we are also proposing a credits/makeup plan where appropriate."
- "Procurement timeline is long": "What are the gating documents they need? We'll provide a compressed packet and a dedicated AE contact to accelerate."

Appendix snippets (cut/paste into deck)
- SLA snapshot: uptime %, P99 latency, credits in last 12 months
- Sample technical runbook: escalation path, alert contacts, expected MTTR for common classes
